transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Partnerships); Liam O'Connor (HelioGrid Head of Partnerships), Dr. Saira Patel (HelioGrid Solutions Architect), Omar Reyes (BizDev)

Summary:
Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and HelioGrid Systems. Topics: HelioGrid's GPU/hardware skus and go-to-market interest for joint offerings, technical compatibility (VPC, private deployments, network topologies), performance expectations (latency/throughput), and partnership model (referral vs co-sell vs OEM). Agreement to exchange SKUs and benchmark data and schedule a SE deep-dive to map integration points and pilot scope.

Topics: partner intro, hardware SKUs, private deployment (VPC/on-prem), dedicated capacity, security/compliance (SOC2/KMS), pilot scope, commercial model

Action items (recap at end in audio): see action_items metadata above

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team.. um Diego our SE is here, and Priya from partnerships is joining — quick round robin — Liam?
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Yeah hi hi, Liam here, thanks for setting this up. We're HelioGrid, we build GPU appliances and rack scale systems focused on inference and mixed workload customers. Saira and Omar are with me.
[00:23] Diego Ramos: Nice to meet you — Diego, I'm the solutions engineer. We're excited to learn about HelioGrid's hardware and where we might partner.
[00:30] Saira Patel: Thanks. Quick note, apologies up front if sometimes I talk in arch diagrams. We do a lot of custom networking for enterprise.
[00:37] Maya Chen: totally expected. Quick agenda: 1) high level HelioGrid business and GTM 2) technical — SKUs, perf numbers, networking 3) where Redwood could integrate (hosted, dedicated, private) 4) next steps

[01:05] Liam O'Connor: We're seeing buyers who want predictable inference costs and low latency — historically they've had to build their own stacks. So we're exploring partnerships with runtimes and cloud-native inference platforms. Co-sell and channel enablement interest.
[01:20] Omar Reyes: Our customers are mid-enterprise to large telco and retail; compliance and data residency are big asks.
[01:28] Priya Singh: That's very aligned. Redwood's been pushing private deployments and dedicated pools — predictable throughput, and private control plane for regulated workloads.

[01:45] Saira Patel: On SKUs: we have three families — H-Series (dense inference GPUs, A100/Next gen equivalents), M-Series (mixed CPU+GPU for multitenant inference), and EdgeBox (small form-factor for on-prem retail). We can share exact SKUs after NDA but high level numbers now..
[02:05] Diego Ramos: Great. Are your H-Series single-tenant racks or multi-tenant capable? How are you handling NVLink / interconnect?
[02:14] Saira Patel: H-Series is rack scale, full NVLink mesh per node, primarily for single-tenant or dedicated capacity. M-Series is for consolidation — has resource slicing and we expose PCI passthrough or MIG-like partitions depending on customer.
[02:30] Maya Chen: Sounds like a good fit with Redwood Dedicated — customers that need predictable throughput could map to H-Series. For multi-tenant we could map to hosted variants or Redwood Optimize suggestions to shard models or quantize.

[02:45] Liam O'Connor: One thing we want to understand is the integration complexity — does Redwood require any kernel-level changes or custom runtime hooks, or is it mostly standard containerized inference?
[02:56] Diego Ramos: Mostly containerized — our serving runtime picks optimized kernels, but the platform is delivered as containers and orchestration. For HelioGrid H-Series we'd likely run Redwood Dedicated in a private cluster with our runtime pinned. There are sometimes driver/solver matrix quirks (CUDA versions, driver compatibility). We do a compatibility pass in onboarding.

[03:18] Saira Patel: That fits. Network — our customers often require VPC peering, private control plane, and on-prem air-gapped options. Are those supported?
[03:27] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. We also have audit logs and RBAC.

[03:40] Omar Reyes: What's the typical onboarding timeline for a dedicated/private deployment?
[03:45] Diego Ramos: For a simple Dedicated deployment on a cloud partner it's weeks. For on-prem or air-gapped private it's usually 6-12 weeks depending on networking and security reviews — certs, SOC2 documentation, KMS integration.

[04:00] Liam O'Connor: Are you seeing customers favoring quantized models (8-bit) to improve density? Because on our hardware density and utilization are key metrics.
[04:10] Maya Chen: yes definitely. Redwood Optimize actually gives model and quantization recommendations by workload and can suggest batching/caching policies to reduce unit cost while preserving quality. We also support kernel selection for quantized paths.
[04:28] Saira Patel: Perfect. From HelioGrid's perspective we'd want to offer a joint package for enterprise customers — Helio hardware + Redwood Dedicated runtime + managed onboarding. Commercial options: referral, co-sell, or OEM pre-install.

[04:43] Priya Singh: All of those are on the table. For go-to-market we typically start with referral and co-marketing, then pilot customers to build a case study.

[05:00] Diego Ramos: On the tech side, a few things to validate in a SE deep-dive: 1) driver/OS matrix, 2) performance benchmarks (latency p95/p99 with typical LLM sizes), 3) KV cache integration and network bandwidth for stateful chat workloads, 4) how safe fallbacks to smaller model variants would be handled when capacity constrained.

[05:25] Saira Patel: We'll share benchmark spreadsheets. We have internal perf runs with Llama2 and a few open models — numbers vary by tensor cores and NVLink config. Expect to share both FP16 and int8 runs.

[05:40] Liam O'Connor: Commercial question — how do you price Dedicated vs Hosted? Is there a revenue share option for partners?

[05:48] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. For partners we do referral fees and can discuss co-sell models — revenue share or discount for pre-bundled offerings. We'll put a partner model in the one-pager.

[06:05] Omar Reyes: Security/compliance — do you provide SOC 2, ISO attestations and audit logs? Customers ask frequently.

[06:12] Maya Chen: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, ISO certs in process for some regions, and we expose audit logs and token-level cost/latency breakdowns. KMS integration available. We'll share the security deck.

[06:30] Diego Ramos: A technical note — if HelioGrid wants to pre-install Redwood Private in their appliances for an OEM offering we'll need a packaging plan. There's also license considerations for our private control plane.

[06:45] Saira Patel: On OEM, we have a hardware enablement team. We'd be interested in the packaging and license model — is the private control plane still Redwood-operated or customer-operated?

[06:56] Maya Chen: It can be customer-operated for on-prem deployments; for a managed OEM we do partner-managed installs. We'll scope the options in the follow-up doc.

[07:10] Liam O'Connor: Another operational piece — telemetry and observability. Our hardware team wants to know resource telemetry we can expose for joint dashboards.

[07:18] Diego Ramos: Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost and latency, per-model dashboards, and tracing hooks. If HelioGrid exposes telemetry (power, GPU utilization, temp) we can integrate into the Console via exporters.

[07:32] Saira Patel: Good — we'll inventory the telemetry endpoints we can expose.

[07:38] [background noise, crosstalk]
[07:45] Priya Singh: On partnership motion — we'll propose a first pilot: one HelioGrid enterprise retail customer who wants a low-latency product search LLM. Pilot scope: 8x H-Series nodes, run Redwood Dedicated, target p95 latency <120ms for 4k context. Thoughts?

[08:00] Liam O'Connor: That aligns to a case study we wanted. We can propose to the customer. They have strict PCI-adjacent requirements so private deployment mandatory.

[08:12] Diego Ramos: That pilot seems realistic. We'll need model selection (open vs proprietary), batching strategy, and KV cache tuning. Also pass/fail criteria — latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens.

[08:28] Saira Patel: We'll provide the customer's network topology — they are on a private ASN and require VPC peering and static routing.

[08:36] Maya Chen: ok good. Next steps recap: Redwood sends partner one-pager and partnership model; HelioGrid shares SKUs and perf numbers; schedule SE deep-dive.

[08:50] Omar Reyes: Quick question — do you support function calling / tooling / structured output for LLMs? Some customers need tight integration with enterprise systems.

[08:58] Diego Ramos: Yes — we support streaming responses, function/tool calling, and structured output. That fits well for e.g., search reranking or structured product metadata extraction.

[09:10] Liam O'Connor: What about model fallback policies? If we oversubscribe dedicated capacity, can Redwood route to hosted or smaller variants automatically?

[09:20] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing with policy-based fallbacks is built-in. You can route by latency, cost, region, or tier and automatically fallback to compatible variants.

[09:31] Saira Patel: On the security side again, what KMS do you integrate with? AWS KMS, Azure? HSM?

[09:38] Maya Chen: We integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and can work with HSM partners for on-prem. We'll share the KMS integration docs.

[09:48] [short pause]
[09:55] Diego Ramos: One more technical ask — for performance validation we'll want raw perf runs (latency microbenchmarks) and a simulated workload trace to match customer traffic. Can HelioGrid provide those traces or should Redwood simulate?

[10:07] Saira Patel: We can provide traces from similar customers, redacted. We'll include a sample in the perf workbook.

[10:16] Priya Singh: Great. I'll coordinate calendars; propose the SE deep-dive week of 12/20.

[10:23] Liam O'Connor: That works. We'll do internal check and share SKUs by 12/16.

[10:30] Maya Chen: Awesome — thanks all. Recap and I'll send the one-pager + partnership model and a calendar invite for the SE deep-dive.

[10:40] Omar Reyes: Thanks, appreciate it.

[10:45] End of call (technical hangups and a few dropped packets around 00:11:30 - brief rewind in recording)

Note on transcription quality: there were a few mis-heard proper nouns (some internal SKU names muffled), and occasional speaker label swaps during brief crosstalk. Overall medium quality recording.

References shared during call: "HelioGrid SKUs (to be shared)"; "Redwood partner one-pager (link to be sent)"; "Perf workbook template (Redwood/HelioGrid)"

Recap (as spoken at end):
- Redwood to send partner one-pager, partnership model, and security deck (Maya)
- HelioGrid to share SKUs, perf runs, and network/topology constraints (Liam / Saira)
- SE deep-dive to be scheduled week of 2026-12-20 (Diego + Saira)
- Pilot scope draft: 8x H-Series nodes for retail product search, target p95 <120ms, private deployment

End transcript.
